newsitem.title: NORWAY: Non-UK North Sea oil output dipped in June - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Non-UK North Sea oil output dipped in June - analyst.

text.p: Production of oil and natural gas liquids (NGL) in the North Sea averaged 5.45 million barrels per day (bpd) in June, down 335,000 bpd, or almost six percent from a month earlier, analysts Wood Mackenzie said on Monday.

Output in northwest European waters -- Norway, Denmark and the Netherlands -- slipped 186,000 bpd in June to average 3.40 million bpd compared with 3.58 million bpd in May, Wood Mackenzie said in a new report.
Norwegian oil/NGL production decreased five percent, or 180,000 bpd, in June to 3.14 million bpd with several fields showing lower throughput.
The greatest decline was at Saga Petroleum's Vigdis field, which was shut in for the whole month due to problems at the gas compressor.
Norsk Hydro's Oseberg and Brage also registered reduced production of around 131,000 bpd and 38,000 bpd respectively due to shutdowns linked to scheduled maintenance.
Wood Mackenzie said the most significant increase in output was at the Gyda field, operated by British Petroleum, which pumped an average 43,000 bpd, the highest output since November, 1996.
Production at Shell's Draugen field recovered to 182,000 bpd following an eight-day scheduled maintenance stoppage in May.

Danish oil/NGL output decreased three percent to an average 229,000 bpd from the record level of 236,000 bpd in May. Wood Mackenzie attributed the slip largely to a seasonal decline in condensate production at the Tyra field.

Production at the Skjold and Svend fields fell 3,000 bpd and 4,000 bpd from May respectively, while the most substantial increase was achieved at the recently onstream Harald field, where pumping rose by 6,000 bpd to 18,000 bpd, the analysts said.
Average oil/NGL production at Dutch fields held a steady 31,000 bpd in June against 30,000 bpd in May.
